title: How to Write a Book Description and Back Cover Blurb (With Examples) | Legenddary's SparkPrep
h1: How to write your book description and back-cover blurb
description: A simple formula for first-time authors: write a book description that sells on Amazon and a back-cover blurb that fits, with KDP's 4,000-character limit, a 150-word target and examples.
platforms: Amazon KDP, IngramSpark, any bookstore listing
lead: After the cover, your description is what makes a stranger buy your book. You don't have to be a marketer. A simple four-part formula works for almost any book.

answer.q: How long should a book description be?
answer.a: Aim for about 150 words, which is what Amazon KDP suggests: short, simple sentences a shopper can scan in seconds. KDP allows 30 to 4,000 characters. Your back-cover blurb is usually the same text trimmed to fit, often 100 to 200 words, leaving room for the barcode.

body:
The four-part formula

  1. The hook (1 line). One sentence that makes them curious. "She had one night to forget everything she knew."
  2. The setup (2-3 sentences). Who it's about and what they want. For nonfiction: who the book is for and the problem it solves.
  3. The stakes (2-3 sentences). What stands in the way and what happens if they fail. Don't give away the ending.
  4. The close (1 line). Who'll love it, or a simple invitation: "Perfect for fans of..." or "Start reading today."

An example (fiction)

Nobody in Harlow Creek talks about the summer of 1999. Mara is about to find out why.
When Mara comes home to sell her late father's farm, she finds a box of letters he never sent, all addressed to a girl who vanished the year Mara turned ten. The town wants the past buried. The letters say it isn't finished.
A quiet, twisting mystery for readers who love small towns with big secrets.

Amazon's rules

  • Between 30 and 4,000 characters.
  • KDP suggests keeping it short and simple, about a 150-word paragraph.
  • Leave out contact details and time-limited promotions; KDP's metadata guidelines don't allow them.

From KDP's Write a Book Description and description-writing help topics, checked November 2026.

Turning it into a back-cover blurb

The back cover uses the same words, trimmed to fit. Remember what else lives there:

  • The barcode takes the bottom-right corner (where the barcode goes).
  • Text must stay inside the safe area, away from the edges and spine.
  • Use at least 7-point text (KDP's minimum), and more like 10 to 12 point so it's easy to read.

Your back cover is the same size as your front. Find yours in the book cover dimensions chart, or start from a free template.

Quick checklist

  • Does the first line make you want the second?
  • Is it clear what kind of book it is in 5 seconds?
  • Short paragraphs, no spoilers, no typos?
  • Does the back-cover version fit around the barcode with room to spare?

Once the words are ready, SparkPrep, an Automated Publishing Production System (A.P.P.S.), checks the finished cover for text near the edge, the barcode area and the 7-point minimum, alongside the rest of the file.

faq.q: What is the difference between a blurb and a book description?
faq.a: They're usually the same text. The book description is what shows on Amazon and other stores; the blurb is the version printed on the back cover, often trimmed to fit around the barcode.

faq.q: How many characters can a KDP book description have?
faq.a: Between 30 and 4,000 characters, including spaces and punctuation. KDP suggests aiming for about a 150-word paragraph.

faq.q: Should I put reviews on my back cover?
faq.a: Only real quotes you have permission to use. Never make up reviews. A first book can skip them and let a strong blurb do the work.
